input.headline: Skip the 22-miler: an 18-miler with 4 miles at marathon pace gives the same race practice in under 3 hours. Keep the week near 45 miles and keep the easy miles easy so the race-pace work lands.
input.analysis:
## What last week showed
Last week went to plan. All five runs were completed, the threshold session was three 2-mile reps at 7:58/mi with a fade under 1 percent, and the long run was the full 17 miles. Nothing was skipped and nothing was overrun.

## Why the easy share was low
Only 61 percent of your time was in zones 1 and 2, under the 80 percent target. The cause was the long run, which averaged 146 bpm and spent 57 percent of its time in zone 3, so it ran harder than easy. Holding the easy miles near 145 bpm fixes this without changing the plan.

## Why an 18 and not a 22
Three weeks out from the race, the long run's job is to rehearse race effort, not to add distance. A 22 at easy pace would take close to 3 hours 40 minutes, and the fatigue would linger into the taper. The 18 with four miles at marathon pace gets the race practice in under 3 hours.

## Pace discipline
Marathon pace for a 3:45 finish is 8:35/mi. Your threshold reps at 7:58/mi show you can run faster than that, and the risk now is running the race-pace miles too fast and paying for it on race day.

## The load this week
Forty-five miles is about 7 percent more than last week. The hard work sits in two sessions, Wednesday and Sunday, with easy days between them, so the recovery pattern holds. Volume should come down over the next two weeks so you reach the start fresh.

## The race-date worry
You said you are anxious about the new date. The pull is to add miles to feel ready, and that is the one thing I would avoid now. The plan already holds the work you need, and the easy and rest days matter as much as the runs.
input.plan:
Mon Sep 28: rest. Full day off so last weekend's 17 miles can settle before this week's work.
Tue Sep 29: easy, 6 mi, about 9:50/mi and under 145 bpm on flat ground. Keeps the legs moving after the long run without adding stress.
Wed Sep 30: quality, 9 mi: 2 mi easy, 5 mi at 8:35/mi marathon pace, 2 mi easy. This is the first race-pace session of the peak, so run the 8:35 miles at that pace, not faster.
Thu Oct 1: easy, 8 mi, about 9:55/mi and under 145 bpm. This is the mid-week medium-long run; keep it truly easy so the weekend stays fresh.
Fri Oct 2: rest. Full rest before the long run.
Sat Oct 3: easy, 4 mi, about 10:00/mi. A short shakeout that keeps the rhythm before tomorrow's long run.
Sun Oct 4: long, 18 mi: first 10 mi at about 9:55/mi, then 4 mi at 8:35/mi, then 4 mi at about 9:55/mi, easy miles under 145 bpm. It stays under 3 hours, and the marathon-pace miles rehearse race effort on tired legs.
input.flags:
Pace discipline: Marathon pace for a 3:45 finish is 8:35/mi, and your threshold reps ran 7:58/mi, so hold back on the race-pace miles.
Easy share low: Only 61 percent of time was in zones 1 and 2 because the 17-mile run averaged 146 bpm, so keep the easy miles near 145 bpm.
Race-date anxiety: You said you feel anxious about the new date, and adding miles to feel ready is the risk, so stick to the plan.
Load step up: This week is 45 miles against 42 last week, so if the legs feel heavy on Thu Oct 1, cut the medium-long run to 6 mi.</flags>
<parameter name="answers">No, skip the 22. A 22 is not needed to get under 3:45, and it would cost recovery time you need before race day.
